title: Sleepers and Expert Targets
brief: Which players do the experts expect to beat their price in our format, tiered by expected cost? Each line must give the reason (overlooked team, role, market overreaction) so we know how far to bid.
summary: The experts' biggest edges sit in the middle of our auction, roughly picks 51 to 100. There, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Dejounte Murray, Ryan Rollins, Damian Lillard and Paul George sell far below what the experts think they are worth. Bid above the market's average cost but stay under the expert ceiling given in each line, and only chase gaps of 15 spots or more. Most discounts come from three places: Jazz players, starters whose job is in doubt, and injury or age risk that the price already reflects.

sections.heading: Bid between the market and the expert value

paragraphs.text: Rankings and projections tell you how good a player is. ADP and average cost tell you what the market will pay. The rule is simple: if you rank a player 30th and his ADP is 70th, take him in the 50s. In our auction, that means bidding above the market's average cost but below the expert value. You still get the player, and you keep part of the edge. Nickeil Alexander-Walker shows how this works. Experts call him free money at his market cost, and Josh values him in the mid 20s USD, but the target range is 15 to 20 USD.

Only chase big gaps. A gap of a few spots leaves no room for error. A gap of 15 to 20 spots still protects you if the player underperforms. Leagues are won by players who jump about 40 spots above where they were drafted. The best value usually sits between picks 51 and 100, where players can beat their ADP by 10 to 40 spots. In our 144-player draft, that is the middle of the auction. Many expert targets sit there: Dejounte Murray (experts say top 50, ADP about 70), Ryan Rollins (picks 50 to 65), Zach Edey (picks 60 to 70) and Ty Jerome (picks 74 to 80).

Check our own room's history before you bid. Last season our league paid far more than today's market price for Anthony Davis, Domantas Sabonis, Jalen Williams, Dyson Daniels and Ivica Zubac. It paid almost nothing for Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Keyonte George, Zach Edey and Jaden McDaniels. Expect someone to bid on last year's names. Do not follow them past the expert ceiling in each line.

Overlooked team. Players on teams nobody watches often go cheap. The fantasy community is still skeptical of Jazz players after the tanking years, and experts expect that to create big discounts. Three Jazz players are expert targets. Lauri Markkanen gives elite FT% on volume. Jaren Jackson Jr. is ranked about 36th in categories by experts. Keyonte George is worth about 20 USD to experts. All three share one ball, so in the first weeks check how much usage each keeps next to Darryn Peterson.

Role doubt. When drafters fear a player will lose his starting job or share minutes, his price drops. That is value only if you believe he starts. This applies to CJ McCollum (versus Dort), Ryan Rollins (versus Porter and Burries), Day'Ron Sharpe (needs 24 or more minutes), Neemias Queta (versus Mitchell Robinson) and Quentin Grimes (versus LaRavia). Bid only at the prices in their lines. Check starts and minutes in the first two weeks, and cut quickly if the role is not there.

Injury and age risk. These players can be good value when the discount is large, because the price already includes the risk. The market prices in Kyrie Irving's ACL. Anthony Davis is a top-20 per game player who will miss games. Jalen Suggs should be planned for about 20 missed games. Zach Edey carries injury risk. LeBron James will sit some games for rest. Pay the discounted price, not the healthy price. For example, 26 to 30 USD is fair for Davis, but paying near his ESPN value or last season's price in our room is not.

The experts agree on who is underpriced but not always on the ceiling. On Kevin Durant, experts take him late in round one, while Josh found 40 USD too rich. On Zach Edey, Josh caps his bid at 11 USD, while other expert bids go up to 20 USD. On Trey Murphy III, Lloyd is fine taking him at pick 20, while Josh says mid 20s USD because he slid. His profile warns that above 25 USD you pay for a role he had with Murray out. On Lauri Markkanen, the experts grade him round 3 and a mid-20s USD bid fits, but one mock already went to 30 USD. On Ajay Mitchell, one expert calls his ESPN rank laughable and others disagree. When the experts split like this, bid at the lower number and let the room decide whether to go higher.

sections.heading: Playoff weeks and the trade deadline

paragraphs.text: Strong schedules in weeks 19 to 21 add value. Memphis plays 4-4-4, which helps Zach Edey and Ty Jerome. Dallas also plays 4-4-4, but Kyrie Irving only gains if he does not sit back-to-backs. New Orleans plays 4-4-3, which helps Dejounte Murray and, if he holds a real role, Jeremiah Fears.

Weak schedules mean a sell plan before the 2027-03-04 deadline. The notes flag a weak schedule for Miami (4-3-3), Houston, Indiana (3-4-3), Portland, the Knicks and Brooklyn. Minnesota has a two-game semifinal week, Cleveland has a two-game finals week, and Philadelphia has three back-to-backs. Golden State may fade late in the season. Draft Damian Lillard, OG Anunoby, Brandin Podziemski and Yaxel Lendeborg as players you may trade before the deadline. Do not pay extra for Amen Thompson, Ivica Zubac or Michael Porter Jr. because of their March value.

The last picks of our 144-player draft are where 1 to 2 USD flyers belong. The experts like Peyton Watson, Egor Dëmin, Quentin Grimes, Jeremiah Fears, Yaxel Lendeborg, Ajay Mitchell, Gui Santos, Cameron Johnson, Grayson Allen and Paul Reed there. Do not bid more than 2 USD on any of them. Each one depends on a starting role or a breakout. If the role is not there in the first two weeks, drop him and use FAB instead.

Cheap starting centers are the best late value for punt 3PM builds. Neemias Queta, Isaiah Hartenstein and Jakob Poeltl all help FG% and rebounds for a few USD. Our room paid much more for Hartenstein and Poeltl last season, so expect them to cost less this time. Check minutes early: 26 or more for Queta, 28 to 29 for Hartenstein and 28 for Poeltl.
